desert_p07_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_001.text: The first cairn stood on the ridge path, built around a dark upright slab. Its broken partner appeared farther east, above a shallow fall of pale rubble. Tuo stopped between them with one hand shading her eyes. She had always called them the split cairn, as did most carriers. From here they looked less like halves of one monument than two markers whose separate purposes had been forgotten. Gao asked Yue to draw their positions before approaching the eastern one. Du unfolded the oldest site sheet.

desert_p07_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_002.text: Its single black dot occupied neither exact place, a useful symbol that had hidden an awkward distance. They could see the lower exchange from the western cairn, though little of it rose above the deposited salt dust. Three narrow openings faced the east, matching the subscriber sketch. A northern stair descended beside a flat surface most travellers would have taken for road. Its outer edge continued beneath the ridge debris. Tuo pointed out the old loading apron, then frowned at how its line vanished. Years of wind had laid material against the walls. The building had not disappeared through sorcery.

desert_p07_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_003.text: It had become easier to overlook each season, until a map name did more visible work than its roof.

desert_p07_004.speaker: du_she
desert_p07_004.text: There should be a balance carved over the middle opening. I cannot see it from here. The upper station has the wind inscription, the lower one the scale. That would settle the caption if the carving survives. Gao, let me carry the older sheet where you can reach it. My fingers are trying to fold it toward what I hope to find, which is a disgraceful way to perform evidence. Yue, your sketch shows the two cairns better than this dot. Put the eastern one beside the ridge notch, not beside our expectation of a broken twin.

desert_p07_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_005.text: Gao measured the bearing from the western marker to the visible lower openings. Du's sheet fitted after allowing for the coarser scale. The eastern cairn carried a faint horizontal cut, unlike the western slab's upright notch. Tuo walked along the firm path toward it while the others packed the sighting glass. Her staff found hard stone for three steps, then a thin crust near the rubble edge. She withdrew the staff and moved to avoid it. The next piece of apparently sound paving shifted under her heel, tilting toward a hollow she had not seen.

desert_p07_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_006.text: Tuo's left foot dropped only a short distance, but the twist threw her toward the loose edge. Du caught her forearm while Gao planted the sighting staff across the sound paving. Yue moved the instrument case clear, leaving the stable patch open for their feet. Tuo took her own weight on the staff and drew the trapped foot back. A little spill of grit fell into the hollow. They stood without speaking until she found a secure stance. Du was breathing hard.

desert_p07_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_007.text: His hand remained around her arm after the immediate need passed, as though he had to persuade himself of its solidity.

desert_p07_008.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p07_008.text: Let go, Du. I am here. I promise not to vanish merely to prove your hand useful. Gao, the ankle hurts, but I can stand on the right foot. We will go back along the path we have just used. No, I do not need to inspect the lower door before resting. You may record that admission somewhere permanent if it gives you pleasure. Yue, fetch my staff from the gravel beside the loose slab. Leave the slab alone. It has offered enough commentary on my morning without our asking it to speak more clearly.

desert_p07_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_009.text: Yue fetched the staff from firm ground while Gao checked Tuo's balance. The guide could put a little weight on the left foot, though the movement hurt. Returning to camp was the sensible next task. Du offered an arm, then reconsidered how narrow the path became. They moved in short stages with Tuo using the staff, Gao ahead and Du beside her on the wider portions. Yue carried both light cases. Her palms stayed clear of rough grips. Behind them, the cairn remained upright and indifferent.

desert_p07_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_010.text: The small fall had not changed its shape, only their willingness to read the ground around it. On the ridge Tuo stopped to breathe and looked toward the lower roof. She had been trying to remember an approach from before the northern storms that brought her brother's body home. Memory had supplied a path without the years laid over it. She said that plainly, before Gao asked for a description. Du answered that the paving was undermined beneath a surface any of them might have trusted. Both things could be true.

desert_p07_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_011.text: Tuo accepted his words without using them to escape her own judgement. The work had become less forgiving of memory, not more charitable to pride. They took longer returning than they had walking out. Crescent House's broad arch appeared between the dark stones, its singing softer in the morning air. Bao saw the altered pace and met them before Tuo reached the forecourt. The clinician brought a seat and examined the ankle in shade. Swelling had begun along the outer side, but no obvious deformity appeared. The guide could move her toes and feel Bao's touch.

desert_p07_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_012.text: A fuller assessment would follow after rest; for now she would not guide the afternoon walk. Tuo opened her mouth to argue, then looked at Du's still-shaking hand and closed it.

desert_p07_013.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p07_013.text: You will put the foot up. I shall examine it again after the swelling settles a little. Ice is a lovely idea in the wrong place, so we shall use a cool damp wrap from the treatment portion and ordinary rest. Your staff has earned an afternoon beside your chair. If they need a route explanation, they can ask while you are seated. Do not begin teaching us a new technique for guiding on one leg. I know you are inventive. I would prefer you exercise that talent on the question of how to remain comfortable until lunch.

desert_p07_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_014.text: Tuo complained that Bao sounded pleased. The clinician said people who obeyed the first instruction made her practically festive. Han came over, heard the account, and asked whether they should leave before another part of the site collapsed. Gao described the limited incident and the remaining safe overlook. The caravan camp remained on the checked gravel strip. Returning required Tuo's judgement of the road, which she could give while resting, and the drivers' steady work. The injury did not automatically make a hurried departure safer. Han looked at the elevated foot and admitted haste had become an unattractive argument.

desert_p07_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_015.text: The camp worker offered Tuo his folded cloak as a cushion. She accepted, then apologised for taking something from a man with his own restricted wrist. He said the cloak used neither wrist unless it attempted to tie itself. The joke pleased her enough to stop the apology. Yue brought the map table nearer so she could point at the ridge path without standing. Du sat at its far end. He had scraped his knuckles against stone while catching her. Bao cleaned the marks, and Tuo watched the treatment with an expression more difficult than gratitude.

desert_p07_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_016.text: Years of argument did not prepare a person for being held upright by its object. Du did not speak about his knuckles. He asked which lower-site path Tuo had used before the storms. She showed a line west of the eastern cairn, now partly buried. A safer modern approach followed the ridge farther north before descending. It would add walking but avoid the undermined apron. Gao could inspect it from visible rock, with the farrier accompanying the next small group to help assess ordinary footing. Han would remain by the carts.

desert_p07_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_017.text: The plan did not require Tuo to prove the value of her old knowledge by repeating the painful step. She seemed relieved by that distinction.

desert_p07_018.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p07_018.text: Your memory still tells us where the paths were. We can place today's ground beside it without making either pretend to be the whole account. I want the northern approach described while you rest. Then I shall go only as far as sound footing gives us a view. Yue has the present positions of the cairns; Du has the older sheet. We can locate the lower building without carrying you down to it. If the next look shows the loading apron has lost support, that is a result, not a failure to complete the report.

desert_p07_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_019.text: Tuo traced the northern descent with a blunt pencil. At its first bend a black outcrop should rise beside a low dry wall. The wall could have fallen; the outcrop would remain. The path then reached a ledge above the three eastern openings. Gao wrote both features and the uncertainty. Yue watched the guide work from her chair, exact now in what she remembered and what she did not. Pain made her impatient but not foolish. Du slid his map closer when she needed another scale. They did not exchange a reconciliatory speech. The papers moved between them without resistance.

desert_p07_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_020.text: Han asked Bao whether the ankle injury changed the water use forecast. She expected a small treatment portion but no large new need if Tuo rested in shade. He added that to the day's actual column as it was used. The first tank's frame remained dry; the drivers had checked its joints after the descent. Their ordinary tasks continued beside the unexpected ones. Yue found comfort in that continuity. The world had not reduced itself to Tuo's foot, yet her foot mattered enough to change the work. A crew could hold both scales without choosing one as the true story.

desert_p07_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_021.text: While Gao prepared the afternoon cases, Du stood outside the arch with Tuo's recovered staff. He had not realised he still held it. Yue pointed to the empty place beside her chair, and he looked embarrassed before carrying it back. Tuo thanked him directly this time. He said the staff belonged where she could reach it. She answered that she had meant the arm, not the staff. For a moment he seemed incapable of accepting the simplest words. Then he nodded and sat down.

desert_p07_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_022.text: Yue moved away with the field book, giving them space that did not need to become an announced favour.

desert_p07_023.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p07_023.text: You came with paper when I wanted my brother, and I spent years treating you as though paper were all you could bring. That was unfair. It was also true that you spoke badly that first day. I am not withdrawing every old complaint merely because you caught my arm. I am saying thank you for catching it, and for letting me keep the complaints without asking them to become a debt paid by your scraped hand. We are too old to turn a decent gesture into a complete account of our lives. Sit still while Bao's dressing stops bleeding.

desert_p07_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_024.text: Du said he would preserve at least three of her complaints as a sign of mutual respect. Tuo laughed, then winced when her foot shifted against the cushion. He adjusted it with the awkward care of a man more accustomed to moving paper. She told him the first attempt was wrong and the second better. He accepted instruction without defending his age. Through the arch the northern grille made a low note. They listened until the next gust cut it off. Their friendship had not become uncomplicated.

desert_p07_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_025.text: It had acquired a place where gratitude could sit beside history without either needing to leave. Yue helped the cook prepare lunch because the survey walk had paused. He asked her to sort the dried greens while he measured grain. Some stems were too woody for the short cooking, so she set them aside for a longer stew. The meal had its own decisions, each smaller than a loading apron and capable of improving the afternoon. He asked what the lower building looked like. She described the three openings and the roof almost buried in drift.

desert_p07_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_026.text: He said old kitchens often hid more below the floor than the people paying for them suspected. She asked whether that included secret recipes. He said mostly mice. The driver with the wooden bird returned from checking the road beyond camp. He had gone only to the visible bend with the quiet driver, as Tuo asked, and found no fresh wash across the return track. Its gravel remained firm. They brought back one loose white stone shaped approximately like a fish. The quiet driver offered it to Yue after hearing the shoemaker's request.

desert_p07_027.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_027.text: She examined its blunt tail and smooth side, delighted by a promise completed with somebody else's attention. The stone fit easily in her palm. It would require no cart, no title, and no heroic account. Yue put the fish stone in her habitual pack, separate from Gao's samples. Its purpose was a gift, not proof about the basin. The distinction felt unexpectedly important after days spent converting places into observations. She could carry an ordinary object simply because a child had asked. Han saw it and said his daughter would have requested a whole shoal.

desert_p07_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_028.text: Yue replied that she had been warned against accumulating nephews' rocks. He looked startled, then recognised his daughter's contribution to the story. The laugh that followed sounded like home briefly finding him beside a roof that had forgotten its own inhabitants. Gao ate before the afternoon inspection rather than letting preparation consume the meal. She explained the revised small group: herself, Du, Yue, and the farrier. Tuo would describe from camp; Bao would remain with her and the others. The carts stayed in their checked position.

desert_p07_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_029.text: Han wanted a signal for an early return if the foot worsened or wind changed. Gao chose the camp's red flag raised above the broad arch, visible from the first northern ledge. Yue would check that sightline before descending. The plan gave everyone a simple way to interrupt without chasing voices through stone. The farrier brought a short probing rod from his ordinary kit and left the hammer with a driver. He could identify surface support and recent animal tracks; he was not there to declare an entire underground roof fit for freight.

desert_p07_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_030.text: Gao made that scope plain once, then let him do his work. Tuo told him the gravel at the northern descent sometimes rolled over hard clay. He said he would prefer stone. She replied that the ground rarely supplied a complete list of preferences. The exchange sounded almost cheerful, which Bao took as a useful sign that the pain was manageable. Before they left, Tuo asked Yue to show her the two cairns again in the sketch. Their spacing helped the guide see why her old single-marker description had confused people.

desert_p07_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_031.text: She dictated the northern approach's turns onto a separate page, not over the present plan. Yue wrote exactly which were remembered landmarks. The guide examined the result, changed one direction, and signed the description. A patient in a chair could still contribute a precise piece of work. Yue handed the page to Gao and felt their expedition become stronger through correction rather than through anyone pretending the morning had gone as intended. At the arch Du hesitated, looking back at Tuo. She told him to go before he turned concern into a form of supervision.

desert_p07_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_032.text: He obeyed with a dignity both knew was invented. Yue followed Gao onto the ridge path, her staff making a steadier sound now that she had learned the angle. The farrier walked last, watching the lower ground rather than the broken house. Behind them Han raised the red flag briefly for the sightline test. Yue could see it clearly from the first ledge. She raised her own hand, then watched the cloth lower again. The northern path passed above the cairns before turning toward the exchange. From that height the difference between the markers became unmistakable.

desert_p07_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_033.text: The western slab aligned with Crescent House's entrance; the eastern horizontal cut faced the lower site's loading apron. Du stopped to draw the two sightlines. He had assumed the dot represented one broken structure. The older engineers had marked two work approaches. Wind, coarse copying, and a convenient local name had joined them. Gao asked whether the relation remained exact enough to use. They measured rather than simply admiring the explanation, and found the alignments still visible within their working tolerance.

desert_p07_034.speaker: du_she
desert_p07_034.text: We should call them the paired cairns in the report and include the name travellers use. Otherwise someone will search for our splendidly correct name and miss the place entirely. The word split can remain, provided it no longer suggests one stone broken in half. There is kindness in keeping an old name, and carelessness in letting it carry an explanation it never promised. Yue, show both positions large enough to read. If the printer complains that two marks make the sheet crowded, I shall offer him the choice of crowding paper or crowding travellers onto the wrong approach.

desert_p07_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_035.text: The farrier found the black outcrop Tuo remembered. The dry wall beyond it had lost its upper courses, leaving a low line of stones partly covered by drift. The northern path stayed on the outcrop's exposed base rather than crossing the undermined loading apron. Gao checked where it descended and marked a firm stopping place. From there all three openings were visible. A balance carving survived above the middle one, just as Tuo had said. Du let out a long breath before copying it. The subscriber sketch belonged to this building.

desert_p07_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_036.text: Their morning stumble had delayed the answer without changing its truth. Yue could see a rectangular panel set low beside the northern stair. Dust covered most of its face, but a glass strip showed through, divided by pale lines. It resembled a measuring gauge rather than a window. Gao noted its position and chose not to reach across the soft apron to clean it. A sound side ledge might offer access from the north. The farrier inspected that ledge while the others remained above.

desert_p07_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_037.text: The ridge shaded it, and its stone was part of the exposed outcrop rather than a loose paving cover. He called Gao over for a closer look. The gauge held a dark line behind the glass. It did not move with wind. Beneath it, an old metal outlet projected from the wall with a capped thread and a small squared handle. Du read the surrounding inscription slowly: roof water, lower store, draw measured. The glass was part of a cistern gauge, its scale partly hidden.

desert_p07_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_038.text: Gao traced the visible inlet channel upward to a roof section buried beneath drift but still continuous with the stone. This was not the bitter seep beside Crescent House. It was a separate engineered store. Nobody yet knew what the water inside had become. Gao called the others back to the firm ledge and stopped the inspection there for the moment. The cistern might hold water worth examining, but its capacity and quality were both unverified. She wanted Bao's field screening kit and the water book before turning a dark line into a usable supply.

desert_p07_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_039.text: Du stayed beside the carving just long enough to copy its last surviving characters. Yue drew the gauge, the outlet, and the roof channel together. The picture showed a possible reason to spend the agreed extra morning. It did not yet pay for an extra day. They returned to camp with that difference intact. Bao listened to the cistern description, then opened a small chemical case from her medical equipment box. She had bought its sealed field-screening sets at the Bitter Wells waterhouse before departure, when the route first mentioned abandoned supplies.

desert_p07_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_040.text: There were six complete sets, enough for limited checks and controls, not a laboratory hidden inside a bag. Gao knew the waterhouse's source inspection method from road work. Bao knew how to interpret its drinking limits. Together they could assess the rain store's ordinary mineral and local contamination hazards, then decide what further treatment would be needed. Nobody described the glass line as salvation. Tuo wanted to see the gauge but accepted a sketch instead. Her ankle had stiffened during rest; Bao found no worsening loss of feeling or movement, though the swelling required continued care.

desert_p07_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_041.text: The guide would ride on a properly checked cart for the first return stretches if needed. Han and the quiet driver examined how that passenger load fitted the equipment cart's reduced water and shifted boxes. They kept the stretcher rails available without deciding Tuo required them. She called the precaution extravagant. Bao said extravagance was easier to tolerate than an unnecessary second fall.

desert_p07_042.speaker: han_xun
desert_p07_042.text: We can afford tomorrow here within the present forecast and still make the return with the protected water intact, provided the road does not grow hotter than expected. We cannot add every interesting day after it. If the cistern proves usable, we discuss what to draw and how long that permits us to remain. If it fails the checks, we leave after the bounded morning work. I want that understood before we start admiring the glass. It is a possible supply. Our tanks are an actual one. I have learned to prefer the latter when arranging people's sleep.

desert_p07_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_043.text: Gao agreed and wrote the departure condition on the work page. She wanted the cistern inspected because a reliable former roof store could affect the carriers' reopening plans. Its water might also explain why the lower building survived while the surrounding road changed. Du wanted the inscriptions copied in their proper relation. Yue wanted to hear what a useful water finding sounded like before it became a map symbol. The reasons differed, but the first steps were shared: inspect the visible inlet, read the gauge's surviving scale, and obtain a sample without entering the buried chamber.

desert_p07_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_044.text: Bao carried the chemical case herself while the farrier took a clean jar from the medical box. Han came to the northern overlook this time, leaving the drivers with the carts and Tuo at the map table. Yue walked beside Gao, remembering where the return flag would appear. They stayed on the northern approach, avoiding the loose slab that had hurt the guide. The exchange's balance carving emerged sharply in the lower afternoon light. Beneath it, a scratched line of old numerals marked the height of the loading floor. Drift had buried everything below that reference.

desert_p07_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_045.text: At the gauge ledge Gao brushed dust from the panel using her own dry cloth, keeping grit away from its capped outlet. The glass stood behind a protective metal frame. Its lower scale indicated storage above the draw tap; a separate note described the sump beneath it. Du read the quantity labels against a conversion table in his station manual. The estimated total was about two hundred and seventy litres, with some below the outlet and inaccessible without opening the chamber. It remained an estimate until actual draws were measured. Yue wrote that word where nobody could overlook it.

desert_p07_046.speaker: du_she
desert_p07_046.text: The old unit here is the district water measure, not the flask used in that carrier letter. This table explains the difference. I am grateful to whoever engraved the full caption; it has survived more copying errors than I have. The line suggests a modest store, not a lake beneath the roof. We shall compare it with the measured draw before using the number in any account. Yue, put the gauge height in the sketch as well. If its mechanism is stuck, the handsome quantity may be describing the last season in which it moved.

desert_p07_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_047.text: Gao checked whether the gauge responded to a small test draw. The cap loosened after the farrier cleaned its outer thread with a brush from his kit. The squared handle required a wrench that fitted from the cart repair box; Han had brought it at Gao's request. He opened the valve gradually while Bao held the first jar below. Water ran cloudy for a moment, then clearer. The glass line descended by a visible small amount. Gao closed the handle before taking more. They had confirmed movement, not accurate volume or drinking quality.

desert_p07_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_048.text: The first flush belonged in the inspection record, not a cup. Bao examined the jar against white cloth and measured a portion into the screening vessels. Fine sediment settled at the bottom. The water smelled of stone, with no sharp oily odour. Neither observation was enough. She prepared the mineral checks with Gao keeping the control samples separate. One sealed reference portion came from the waterhouse with the reagent sets. Yue copied times and labels while Han watched the dark line behind glass. The scene lacked the grandeur Du's travel essays might have promised.

desert_p07_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_049.text: It held people bent over small vessels, using their limited tools to ask whether an ordinary substance could safely become extraordinary relief. The first screen showed salts within the kit's ordinary drinking range, much lower than the bitter seep near Crescent House would suggest. The other local hazard checks needed their full reaction time. Bao set them in shade and asked nobody to decide by colour before the controls matured. Gao inspected the exposed inlet channel from the sound ledge. It ran from a surviving stone roof catchment rather than the quarry spill.

desert_p07_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_050.text: A raised lip separated it from the salt apron. The buried roof still had to be located more exactly before they could exclude an obvious surface contamination path. Han looked across the deposited drift toward the surviving roof edge. He had imagined abandoned buildings as empty costs, either worth repairing or best left alone. This one retained a practical thing the road might need. He asked Gao whether reopening the station would require more than clearing its approach. She pointed to the undermined loading apron, damaged access, and unknown chamber structure. A cistern was not a whole functioning stop.

desert_p07_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_051.text: He nodded slowly. The carriers' proposal had been written as if a name on a sheet could be reopened by sending a cart there. The physical place was answering with a longer list. Yue saw a narrow inscription below the gauge that Du had not yet copied. Its first line named emergency road use; the second assigned routine maintenance to the former district station keeper. The store had been built for travellers as well as staff. Du read the damaged final line as a request to leave a recorded remainder where possible.

desert_p07_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_052.text: He marked two uncertain characters rather than restoring them confidently. Bao looked from the words to their sample jars. Han said they would consider the remainder after finding how much usable water could actually be drawn. A century-old request had entered a present argument. The sun lowered behind the ridge, giving the ledge a chill after the day's reflected heat. Bao packed the reacting samples for a careful return to camp, retaining the controls alongside them. Gao closed and recapped the outlet, checking that it stopped leaking.

desert_p07_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_053.text: The measured flush and sample water totalled a small amount, entered separately from the gauge estimate. None had entered the caravan tanks. Yue carried the clean jar while Han carried the wrench. Returning along the path, they could see Tuo's red flag resting low beside the arch. Its stillness gave the waiting camp a particular kind of welcome. Tuo wanted the results before the roof story. Bao said the first salt check was encouraging, while the complete decision would wait for all screens and source inspection. The guide accepted the answer more easily than Han expected.

desert_p07_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_054.text: She had drunk from too many differently named holes to consider a promising taste a contract. Du showed her the emergency-use inscription. She read his uncertain characters, supplied one plausible alternative, and let it remain uncertain when the strokes could support either. Their interpretation would travel with a copy of the actual letters, allowing somebody else to disagree without first finding the gauge ledge. The cook asked how much boiling might be needed if they used the store. Bao said clear, chemically acceptable water still required treatment before drinking.

desert_p07_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_055.text: His charcoal sacks held enough if they measured the batches and kept the stove well shielded. Filtering could remove the loose sediment; it would not remove dissolved salt. That was why the mineral screen came first. He examined the larger kettle and asked Han to reserve the clean storage vessels instead of filling them with tomorrow's wash water. The preparations stayed conditional. The crew would not consume fuel merely to make rejected water look reassuringly hot. Yue helped count the charcoal sacks against their marked weights. Their cooking use had left a known amount, written by the cook each evening.

desert_p07_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_056.text: He disliked writing, but disliked finding an empty sack more. The new water task would need an actual fuel allotment after the first controlled batch. He showed her the stove's close-fitting lid and the folding metal wind shield issued with it. The reed-mat offcut from the village stood farther away, sheltering the eating place rather than touching the fire. Small distinctions kept useful objects from being mistaken for interchangeable ones. Bao rechecked Tuo's ankle after supper. Its movement remained limited by pain and swelling, but no new warning sign required immediate evacuation.

desert_p07_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_057.text: She would keep it raised and avoid the morning walk. Tuo said she had become a landmark herself. Du answered that she was considerably less stable than the dark outcrop and better at arguing. The joke landed gently because he had waited for Bao's judgement. Yue brought the guide a warmer wrap for the cool air. Tuo accepted it, her impatience exhausted for the moment. The camp worker adjusted the chair shade line without needing anyone's praise. Gao drew the buried roof's likely outline from the visible edges and the station manual's standard plan. She kept the inferred portions dotted.

desert_p07_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_058.text: Tomorrow's source inspection would compare those lines with the exposed stone, staying off unknown loading surfaces. The farrier could accompany her for footing, while Du and Yue copied the gauge inscriptions. Han would arrange the return load. Their jobs no longer pointed in every direction at once. The possible water supply gave them a question worth spending the agreed morning on. It did not demand that they solve the whole old district before departing.

desert_p07_059.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p07_059.text: The roof is more important to the sample than it first looks. If its catchment takes ordinary rain and the walls remain sealed against the salt spill, the screening result has a sensible source behind it. If it draws through an old processing floor or an open contaminated channel, we need a different judgement. Our tools answer the hazards they were designed to check. Looking at where the water came from tells us what questions belong beside those answers. Yue, bring the exterior sketch tomorrow. I want the upper channel on the same page as the lower gauge.

desert_p07_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_060.text: Du found a description of the exchange roof in the manual's smaller print. It used a stone catchment above separate storage and service spaces, with dry vents keeping the record room apart from the cistern. The water chamber occupied the northern section. The weighing hall lay beneath the flat loading surface to the east. Later drifting could make both look like ground. He showed Gao the separation, pleased by a design that explained more than a legend would have. She asked him to mark the manual's date. The present building might include alterations the original plan had never known.

desert_p07_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_061.text: Han heard record room and looked at Du with suspicion. The scholar raised both hands, saying he had not asked to enter it. Gao laughed, but admitted records could help identify maintenance and source changes if accessible safely. Tomorrow's work remained outside. Du could copy anything visible through the north opening; he would not cross a broken floor for a desirable page. Yue remembered the injured guide wanting her notebook back and understood the temptation. Paper held reasons, names, and routes. It could matter enormously without becoming worth an uncontrolled fall simply because a reader wanted answers.

desert_p07_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_062.text: The screening controls matured under Bao's lamp. She read them with Gao and entered the results beside the sample labels. The checked mineral and local hazard markers remained within the kit's acceptable limits. That supported further source inspection; it did not turn every possible contaminant into a thing the little case had disproved. The roof store's history and physical isolation would still matter. Bao sealed a retained sample for later examination in Bitter Wells if questions arose. Du wrote the kit type in the report, so the limits of the evidence would survive alongside the encouraging result.

desert_p07_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_063.text: Yue was tired enough to find the glass vessels beautiful. Their small colours held more immediate meaning than the vast basin outside camp. She told Bao that, and the clinician said tired people should admire things from a seat. Yue sat. The older woman had begun a letter to her sister, its first line crossed out twice. She had wanted to write that the journey was ordinary. Two rescued guides and a limping guide made that difficult. Yue offered no wording.

desert_p07_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_064.text: Bao eventually wrote that she was well, working, and looking forward to a kitchen in which every sound belonged to a person. Beyond the treatment lamp Han and Gao considered the next day's return option. One full extra day at the site was still possible from the existing tanks within the cool-weather forecast. A second would require actual usable water, not the estimate. Tuo's ankle might slow walking but could ride where the load check allowed. The drivers would still need sensible rest. They chose a decision time before midday: source inspection first, then measured draw or departure preparations.

desert_p07_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_065.text: Han wrote the time on the page. For once it looked less like a demand and more like a place where worry could stop waiting. Tuo called Yue over after the lamp was lowered. She wanted to see the fish stone. The girl placed it in her hand, and the guide turned it until its blunt tail caught the light. She said her brother once carried a stone like a horse's head for three weeks, promising it to a niece who later called it a potato. Yue asked whether he had kept it. Tuo smiled.

desert_p07_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_066.text: He had given the child a potato too, to clarify the distinction. The memory arrived with laughter this time, requiring no signal cloth and no visible injury to make room for it. Du heard the story and said he remembered the horse stone. Tuo accused him of having drawn it as a coastline in a margin. He produced the old field book from his private case, its pages brittle but protected. The little drawing survived: horse, potato, or an extraordinarily unfortunate peninsula.

desert_p07_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_067.text: They disagreed over it until the driver with the wooden bird offered to ask his daughter as an independent judge. Yue watched Tuo laugh without holding her foot more stiffly. The relief was small and temporary. It was still part of the evening, and nobody asked it to justify itself. The house's singing eased after dark, leaving the lower rushing note more distinct. Gao marked its direction from camp against two positions along the courtyard boundary. It seemed to come from the lower exchange side, though reflections could mislead. She would compare the visible vents tomorrow.

desert_p07_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_068.text: Du left his essay vocabulary alone. Yue carried the lamp, feeling its warmth through the handle wrap. The fieldwork had become a way of meeting the building without forcing it to behave like a story. Her private book would still contain stories. The public page needed positions, conditions, and the patience to leave an uncertain source uncertain. When the day's actual water was closed, one thousand and seventy-seven litres remained in the caravan tanks. The small inspection flush came from the cistern and stayed separate; the tank total had fallen by one hundred and sixty-eight.

desert_p07_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_069.text: Han read the figure once while the cook checked the breakfast grain. The protected compartment remained sealed. Their purchased extra food covered the possible extension, but did not create another water margin by sympathy. Yue heard the number and pictured four return days rather than four blank columns. They were days of feet, heat, animal mouths, and people she knew. The drivers moved Tuo's riding cushion into the equipment cart, securing it without blocking Gao's cases. She objected to the effort until the quiet driver said she had already made it and disliked unmaking good work. Tuo surrendered.

desert_p07_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_070.text: The farrier checked the harness and the six animals under lamplight, asking Long Legs to hold Plum's head while he examined her rear foot. Nothing concerning had developed. The driver thanked him with unaccustomed seriousness. An expedition could survive a report arriving late. A lame mule on the basin ridge would change the practical meaning of every careful plan they had written. Yue settled beside her pack and felt the fish stone through its cloth wrapping. The gift reminded her of the little shop, the shoemaker's girl, and a morning when the largest question was a sandal strap.

desert_p07_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_071.text: Tomorrow would ask about a roof below the ground. The difference was substantial without making that first morning trivial. Her foot still needed the altered strap; her hands still benefited from Bao's patient dressings. The great landscape had been crossed through such details. She let the stone remain wrapped and watched the house window darken beyond the tent's opening. She dreamt of the two cairns standing on opposite sides of a river. One carried a bird's nest, the other a covered cup. In the dream Du tried to put them into the same dot and found his pencil too short.

desert_p07_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_072.text: Yue woke amused rather than frightened. The real cairns were ordinary stones, and ordinary mistakes had given them their confusing name. Her mind was using them for purposes a field report would never accept. She took a drink from the remainder of her evening portion and lay back, letting the dream fade without preserving it as a clue. At dawn Gao spread the exterior sketch beneath a stone so the wind could not turn it over. The north roof catchment, the gauge ledge, and the inferred service chamber now stood on one page.

desert_p07_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p07_073.text: Bao packed the remaining screening sets and the clean collection vessels. Han asked the drivers to keep departure gear ready while the small inspection group worked. Tuo sat with her foot raised, supplying one last description of the northern outcrop. Yue took the light staff and the book. They walked toward the lower exchange in cool shadow, ready to look at what the earth had made easy to mistake for a road.

desert_dilemma_exchange_1.speaker: narrator
desert_dilemma_exchange_1.text: Yue read the formal station label beside Tuo's local name, then asked Du which roof his standard plan described. The plan concerned an earlier arrangement, not a witnessed doorway in today's wall. Matching the building names used the first quiet minutes and left their detailed overlay unfinished. Gao nevertheless knew which uncertainty belonged to age and which belonged to location. Bao kept her sets closed until the water task began. They had spent time identifying the object of the question before trying to answer it.

desert_dilemma_exchange_2.speaker: narrator
desert_dilemma_exchange_2.text: Yue drew the visible wall joints against the older outline and marked every place where the overlay depended on an unseen corner. One attractive access line stopped at a later buttress. Another remained a possibility beyond the observed face. Du folded back the unsupported part of his sheet so nobody would mistake it for a surveyed route. The detailed comparison cost their first rest interval. Gao called the next halt sooner rather than pretending careful desk work had required no concentration.

desert_dilemma_exchange_3.speaker: narrator
desert_dilemma_exchange_3.text: Yue pointed to the plan's likely access and asked Gao to compare it from the permitted ledge. The visible later wall interrupted the proposed line. They withdrew the hypothesis before assigning anyone to follow it, then returned to the northern outcrop with less cool time available. Du wrote the rejected line onto the comparison copy rather than erasing it. A later visitor could see why the appealing route had failed. Bao's screening task still came next; their failed question had bought no extra water.

desert_dilemma_exchange.speaker: narrator
desert_dilemma_exchange.text: On the approach, Gao stopped them within sight of the northern outcrop. The standard plan assumed a service chamber; Yue's exterior sketch showed later walls that might hide its access. They had time for one first comparison before Bao needed the water observations. Yue could establish the building's identity, locate every visible difference, or nominate the plan's most plausible access as a hypothesis. None permitted entry. A wrong first question could consume the cool interval without improving the collection decision. Du waited with the old sheet open.

choices.text: Establish which building each source actually names.
Compare the visible changes before accepting the plan.
Test the old access line as a provisional hypothesis.
